title: Permafrost thaw infrastructure adaptation
bottleneck: Arctic infrastructure — roads, pipelines, buildings, airstrips — was built on permafrost now thawing beneath it, with up to 70 percent of Arctic infrastructure at risk; but adaptation is blocked by unpredictable local thaw rates, the cost of thermosyphon and pile foundations, and the absence of building codes for thawing ground. Abrupt thaw can destroy a roadbed in a single season with no warning. Relocation is often the only durable option, and no funding mechanism exists for it.
why_it_blocks: Thaw damage already costs Arctic communities hundreds of millions annually, threatening Indigenous settlements most. The engineering gap means infrastructure keeps being built to standards for a frozen ground that no longer exists.
current_state: Adaptation techniques — adjustable foundations, passive cooling embankments — work where applied, and permafrost maps are improving. But systematic retrofitting programs and funded relocation pathways remain almost entirely absent.
